steps: 1. Navigate to a page where Logout would normally appear if authenticated
2. Inspect presence and enabled state of the Logout button
test_cases.expected_result: Logout button is not visible or is disabled. No logout action is possible from the anonymous state.

test_cases.test_case: Server-side error during logout shows error and does not clear local session state
preconditions: Simulate server-side logout endpoint returning 500 (or network returns HTTP 5xx)
steps: 1. Trigger logout while server returns a 500 error
2. Observe UI messages and state after the failed logout
test_cases.expected_result: An error message is displayed indicating logout failed (visible notification). The user remains authenticated in the UI (Logout button still shown). Sensitive session data is not partially removed (no inconsistent state).

test_cases.test_case: Click logout while offline results in offline error and no silent session loss
preconditions: Browser network set to offline (no connectivity)
steps: 1. With network offline, click the Logout button
2. Observe UI response and whether session data is cleared
test_cases.expected_result: An offline/network error message is displayed. The UI should not falsely indicate successful logout; Logout button remains visible and user remains in authenticated state until network is restored and logout can complete.

test_cases.test_case: Logout fails when CSRF token missing — UI prevents insecure logout
preconditions: Simulate missing or invalid CSRF token for logout request
steps: 1. Remove or invalidate CSRF token used by the app
test_cases.expected_result: Logout request is rejected by the server; UI displays an error or re-authentication prompt. Session remains active in the client until a secure logout can be completed.

test_cases.test_case: Double-click logout (idempotency) does not cause errors
preconditions: Logout button is visible and enabled
steps: 1. Rapidly click the Logout button twice (double-click)
test_cases.expected_result: Application handles multiple quick logout requests idempotently: user is redirected once to the home page, no duplicate error messages, and no residual authenticated state remains. No UI crash or unexpected behavior occurs.

test_cases.test_case: Logout in one tab invalidates session in another tab (multi-tab behavior)
preconditions: User logged in in two separate browser tabs to the same app
Both tabs have access to protected pages
steps: 2. In Tab B, attempt to navigate to or refresh a protected page
test_cases.expected_result: Tab A redirects to the home page. Tab B, when attempting to access protected content, is redirected to the login page (or shows login prompt). No protected content remains accessible in Tab B after logout in Tab A.

test_cases.test_case: Browser Back after logout does not re-authenticate or show protected data
preconditions: User logged in and on a protected page
Logout completed successfully and user redirected to home page
steps: 1. After logout and redirect to home, click the browser Back button once or multiple times
2. Observe content shown and URL changes
test_cases.expected_result: Using the browser Back button does not re-authenticate the user or display sensitive protected data. Either the browser shows a cached visual but the app detects no session and redirects to the login page, or a non-authenticated version/no content is shown with a prompt to login.
